scenes.title: Examiner's Margin / Household Expenditure
scenes.narration: Welcome to IELTS Winners. This lesson explains how to analyse a household expenditure table and write a strong four-paragraph Task One response. The table compares Canada, Japan, Mexico and Germany, across housing, food, transport and other expenses. We'll identify the key figures, choose the most useful comparisons, and build an overview rather than listing every percentage.

scenes.title: Step 3 / Language Toolkit
scenes.narration: Now let's improve your language. Forty-eight percent is nearly half; twenty-eight percent is slightly over a quarter; twenty-four percent is almost a quarter; twenty percent is a fifth; and ten percent is a tenth. Vary your verbs with account for, comprise, make up, and represent. Use whereas, in contrast, and similarly to link comparisons. Keep the overview focused on the overall pattern.

scenes.title: Steps 4–7 / Grouping, Upgrading and Strategy
scenes.narration: Next, group the data into meaningful comparisons. Pair related categories such as housing and food, then contrast transport and others. Upgrade basic statements by clearly identifying higher and lower shares. Avoid copying the question, repeating figures in the overview, or comparing without a clear purpose. The complete strategy is introduction, overview, body paragraph one and body paragraph two.

scenes.title: Step 2 / Four-Paragraph Response
scenes.narration: Here is the four-paragraph writing plan. First, paraphrase the task. Second, give an overview of the biggest patterns without detailed numbers. Third, compare the higher figures. Fourth, explain the remaining categories using selected percentages. The sample answer demonstrates how each paragraph serves a distinct purpose. Remember: the overview presents main trends, and the two body paragraphs supply supporting comparisons.

scenes.title: Step 1 / Analyse the Table
scenes.narration: Finally, apply the shortcut E R C S: Extremes, Rankings, Comparisons and Spread. Find the highest and lowest figures; identify which category leads in each country; compare similarities and differences; and check how widely values vary. For example, Others reaches forty-eight percent in Japan, while transport accounts for only ten percent there. Select these meaningful observations before writing. That's how you create a clearer, more focused IELTS Task One response.
